recordings.title: How to build durable software with Agentic AI
recordings.speaker: Pavan Kanaparthy
recordings.excerpt: How to build durable software with Agentic AI. Vimeo: https://vimeo.com/1205334343
description: When Claude Code or any coding agent produces a plausible-looking implementation in seconds, the game shifts. The test suite is the only safety net. It's the only thing standing between "looks done" and is done. And if you're a QA professional, that's not a subtle distinction - that's your entire job. Anthropic has been explicit about this: giving an agent a way to verify its own work is the single highest-leverage move you can make in an agentic workflow. That's not a testing philosophy. Today, that is a systems design principle. Comprehensive coverage is how you cash in on it.

recordings.title: Unlocking New Frontiers in Test Automation with AI and Open Source
recordings.speaker: Gregory Goldshteyn
recordings.excerpt: Unlocking New Frontiers in Test Automation with AI and Open Source. Vimeo: https://vimeo.com/1205334342
description: AI is expanding the boundaries of what test automation can achieve. Problems that were once considered impractical—or impossible—to automate are now within reach through advances in large language models, computer vision, and multimodal analysis. This session explores how modern QA teams are building AI-powered test automation capabilities using open-source technologies to validate complex user experiences, dynamic interfaces, and rich media workflows. Attendees will see how AI enables automation beyond the DOM: interpreting visual states, interacting with unstable UIs, understanding streaming playback, analyzing network traffic, and generating tests directly from user behavior. Rather than focusing on theory, the talk highlights concrete AI-driven capabilities and the architectural patterns that make them reusable and extensible across projects. Real-world examples demonstrate how AI can act as an intelligent testing assistant—augmenting existing automation frameworks to increase coverage, reduce manual effort, and accelerate delivery. This session is designed for teams looking to move past incremental improvements and adopt next-generation, AI-enabled automation powered by open source.

recordings.excerpt: Is Today's Test Infra Ready for AI? The Hard Questions No One Is Asking.. Vimeo: https://vimeo.com/1205333889
description: Is Today’s Test Infrastructure Ready for AI? The Hard Questions No One Is Asking AI testing agents are evolving faster than the environments meant to run them. We can now write an autonomous web-test agent, a multimodal workflow bot, or a simulation-driven evaluator — but the moment we try to execute it, we collide with the limitations of traditional test infrastructure. This session challenges a foundational assumption: AI will transform testing. Yes — but only if the underlying infrastructure can support what AI actually needs. Through real scenarios and complex questions, we will explore gaps that most teams don’t realize exist.

recordings.title: AI Generated Test Data: Know Your Need
recordings.speaker: Dr. Bastian Baudisch
recordings.excerpt: AI Generated Test Data: Know Your Need. Vimeo: https://vimeo.com/1205334548
description: If all you have is a hammer, everything looks like a nail: AI continues to transform testing landscapes, promising to drastically reduce complexity and make automation a breeze. Yet, with development speeding up, the availability of realistic, de-identified test data is becoming a bottleneck. On the enterprise scale, AI can neither replace the nuanced reality of production data, nor guarantee compliance. Plus, the organizational challenge of different data consumers (developers, testers, automation engineers, ML engineers) with diverging requirements is often overlooked. Let’s examine the complexities of supplying test data enterprise-wide across departments and diverse environments - tailored to the individual consumers’ needs. I’ll share how to separate technical from organizational complexity and where artificial intelligence can help when employed in the right context.
